paper.title: Active multiple matrix completion with adaptive confidence sets

unmapped: Each 'arm' k is a d_k x d_k matrix of unknown rank r_k; pulling arm k reveals a noisy observation of a uniformly random entry (trace-regression model)
Objective is the estimation loss L_n^p = (sum_k ||M_hat^k - M^k||_F^{2p})^{1/p} after a fixed budget n of samples
Learner knows the dimensions d_k and the bound A on entries and observations, but not ranks or noise variance
Loss parameter p chosen by the learner
settings.definition_quote: At each round the active learner has to choose an action $k_t \in [K]$ and receives a pair $(\bX_t^{k_t},Y_t^{k_t})$ such that $\bX_{t}^{k_t}$ corresponds to the location of the entry ... chosen uniformly at random ... At the end of the game, once it has collected at most $n$ pairs ..., the learner has to output estimates $\hat{\bM}^k_n$ of each matrix $\bM^k$ to suffer the following loss, $\cL_n^p \triangleq(\sum_{k} \|\hat{\bM}^k_n - \bM^k\|_F^{2p})^{1/p}$. ... We further assume that all the observations $Y_{t}^{k_t}$ and the entries of $\bM^k$ are bounded by some known constant $A$.

settings.name_in_paper: Active multiple matrix completion, max loss (lower bound)
unmapped: Each arm k is a d_k x d_k matrix of rank at most r_k; pulling arm k reveals a noisy uniformly random entry
Objective is the max Frobenius estimation loss max_k ||M_hat^k - M^k||_F^2 after budget n
Lower bound holds even if the learner knows the rank bounds r_k and dimensions d_k
settings.definition_quote: For any active strategy $\cS$, there exists a problem $P = (\bM^1, \dots, \bM^K)$, where $\bM^k$ is of rank at most $r_k$ and dimension $(d_k \times d_k)$, such that after $\cS$ (actively) collects at most $n$ observations corrupted with $\cN(0, A^2)$ noise ...

symbols.p_loss: loss parameter p of the L_n^p loss

conditions: entries of each M^k and all observations bounded in absolute value by known A
n >= 48 sum_k d_k log d_k (used in proof)
holds with probability at least 1 - sum_k 16 log(d_k)/d_k
tuning: square-root lasso estimator with lambda = C sqrt(log(d_k)/(d_k T))
loss parameter p given as input

source.label: thm:algoub
source.quote: After $n$ sample requests, {\malocate} started with loss parameter $p$ outputs $K$ estimators, such that with probability at least $1- \sum_k 16\log(d_k)/d_k,$ $\cL_n^p \leq \cO ( (\sum_{k=1}^K (r_k d_k^3 \log d_k )^{\frac{p}{p+1}})^{\frac{p+1}{p}}/n )$

results.notes: Quantity is the L_n^p Frobenius estimation loss, not regret. Paper's n is the budget T. Probability level is non-standard (depends on d_k, not a chosen delta).

conditions: entries and observations bounded by known A
holds with probability at least 1 - sum_k 16 log(d_k)/d_k

source.quote: After $n$ sample requests, {\malocate} started with loss parameter $p=\infty$ outputs $K$ estimators, such that with probability at least $1- \sum_k 16\log(d_k)/d_k,$ $\max_{k\in [K]} \norm{\hat{\bM}^k_n - \bM^k}_F^2 \leq \cO \pa{\frac{\sum_{k=1}^K r_k d_k^3 \log d_k}{n}}$

results.notes: Special case p=infinity of Theorem 1; quantity is the max Frobenius estimation error.

conditions: worst case over matrices M^k of rank at most r_k and dimension d_k x d_k

source.label: thm:lb_max
source.quote: For any active strategy $\cS$, there exists a problem $P = (\bM^1, \dots, \bM^K)$, where $\bM^k$ is of rank at most $r_k$ and dimension $(d_k \times d_k)$, such that after $\cS$ (actively) collects at most $n$ observations corrupted with $\cN(0, A^2)$ noise and outputs $K$ estimators ..., we have $\mathbb E_{P,\cS}[\max_{k \in [K]}(\norm{\widehat{\bM}^k - \bM^k}_F^2)] \geq \frac{A^2}{2048}\frac{\sum_{k=1}^K r_k d_k^3}{n}$

results.notes: Expected max Frobenius estimation loss. Paper notes it holds even for strategies knowing r_k and extends to bounded noise.
